name: Chandelier Exit flip (LeBeau 22/3): long when the ratcheting ATR stop system turns long
rule: Per bar: longStop = ctx.donchian(22,i).upper - 3*ctx.atr(22,i); shortStop = ctx.donchian(22,i).lower + 3*ctx.atr(22,i). Ratchet: if close[i-1] > longStop[i-1] then longStop = max(longStop, longStop[i-1]); if close[i-1] < shortStop[i-1] then shortStop = min(shortStop, shortStop[i-1]). dir[i] = 1 if close[i] > shortStop[i-1]; -1 if close[i] < longStop[i-1]; else dir[i-1] (dir starts at 0). ENTER long when dir changes to 1 from -1 or 0. EXIT when dir changes to -1. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: The Chandelier Exit as plotted on TradingView is a stop-and-reverse trend filter; the registry has only the trailing-stop use of the chandelier (Van Tharp), not its flip signal as the entry.
source: Charles Le Beau and David Lucas, Computerized Trading (1992), chandelier exit; TradingView 'Chandelier Exit' (everget) ratcheting form

name: TRIX(15) signal-line cross: long when TRIX crosses above its 9-period EMA
rule: E1 = EMA15(close), E2 = EMA15(E1), E3 = EMA15(E2), each seeded with the SMA of its first 15 inputs. TRIX[i] = 100*(E3[i]/E3[i-1] - 1). signal = EMA9(TRIX) seeded with the SMA of the first 9 TRIX values. ENTER long when TRIX[i-1] <= signal[i-1] and TRIX[i] > signal[i]. EXIT when TRIX[i] < signal[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: TRIX is a standard triple-smoothed momentum oscillator whose signal-line cross is the usual retail entry; the registry has no TRIX test.
source: Jack Hutson, Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities (1983), TRIX; StockCharts ChartSchool 'TRIX'

name: MACD histogram bullish divergence: lower price low, higher histogram low, confirmed pivot
rule: hist = MACD(12,26,9) histogram (EMA12-EMA26 minus its EMA9). A pivot low at bar p is confirmed at bar p+K when low[p] is strictly below the K lows before and the K lows after it (K=3 here), so it is known only from bar p+K onwards. At the confirmation bar i = p+3 of pivot low p, let q be the previous confirmed pivot low with 8 <= p-q <= 40 (most recent such). ENTER long on bar i when low[p] < low[q] AND hist[p] > hist[q] AND hist[q] < 0 AND hist[p] < 0. EXIT when hist[i] > 0 or after 15 bars in the position. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Regular bullish MACD histogram divergence is one of the most-taught reversal signals; the registry tests RSI hourly divergence and stochastic divergence but not this one.
source: Alexander Elder, Trading for a Living (1993), MACD-histogram divergences ('the strongest signal in technical analysis')

name: Williams %R(14) momentum: long on the cross above -20 while the close is above the 50-day SMA
rule: %R = -100*(HH14 - close)/(HH14 - LL14) with HH14/LL14 = ctx.donchian(14,i).upper/.lower. ENTER long when %R[i-1] <= -20 and %R[i] > -20 and close[i] > ctx.sma('close',50). EXIT when %R[i] < -50. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: The registry tests Williams %R only as an overbought/oversold reversal; reading a push into the top of the range as strength (the Larry Williams trend use) is the untested counterpart.
source: Larry Williams, How I Made One Million Dollars Last Year Trading Commodities (1973); StockCharts ChartSchool '%R'

name: Ichimoku Kumo twist: long when Senkou A crosses above Senkou B (future cloud turns bullish)
rule: mid(n,i) = (ctx.donchian(n,i).upper + ctx.donchian(n,i).lower)/2. A[i] = (mid(9,i) + mid(26,i))/2, B[i] = mid(52,i), both un-shifted (the cloud 26 bars ahead). ENTER long when A[i-1] <= B[i-1] and A[i] > B[i]. EXIT when A[i] < B[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: The Kumo twist is a standard Ichimoku trend-change signal separate from the price-versus-cloud breakouts already tested.
source: Goichi Hosoda, Ichimoku Kinko Hyo (1969); Nicole Elliott, Ichimoku Charts (2007)

name: Kijun-sen cross: long when the close crosses above the 26-bar midpoint line
rule: Kijun[i] = (ctx.donchian(26,i).upper + ctx.donchian(26,i).lower)/2. ENTER long when close[i-1] <= Kijun[i-1] and close[i] > Kijun[i]. EXIT when close[i] < Kijun[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Retail Ichimoku users trade the Kijun cross on its own as a baseline trend line; it is a pure channel-midpoint cross that the full-cloud rules in the registry do not isolate.
source: Goichi Hosoda, Ichimoku Kinko Hyo (1969); Nicole Elliott, Ichimoku Charts (2007) 'Kijun-sen cross'

name: Parabolic SAR flip confirmed by the MACD histogram within three bars
rule: Wilder SAR with step 0.02, max 0.2, started bullish at the first bar with SAR = the first low and EP = the first high; a flip to bullish happens on the first bar where low > SAR, flip to bearish where high < SAR (standard recursion, SAR bounded by the two prior lows/highs). MACD histogram = (EMA12 - EMA26) - EMA9 of that. ENTER long on bar i when SAR is bullish on i, it flipped bullish on one of bars i-2..i, and histogram[i] > 0. EXIT when SAR flips bearish. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: SAR-plus-MACD is a standard retail double-confirmation recipe; plain SAR flips are already in the registry so this asks whether the second indicator adds anything.
source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); common retail 'Parabolic SAR + MACD' systems

name: Smoothed Heikin-Ashi: green run on candles built from EMA(6)-smoothed OHLC
rule: sO,sH,sL,sC = ctx.ema(field,6) of open, high, low, close. haC[i] = (sO+sH+sL+sC)/4; haO[i] = (haO[i-1]+haC[i-1])/2, seeded at the first bar where the EMAs exist with (sO+sC)/2. green = haC > haO. ENTER long when green on bar i and not green on i-1. EXIT when haC[i] < haO[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Smoothed Heikin-Ashi is the common fix retail traders apply to the whipsaw of plain Heikin-Ashi flips, which are in the registry unsmoothed.
source: TradingView 'Smoothed Heikin Ashi Candles' scripts; Dan Valcu, Heikin-Ashi: How to Trade without Candlestick Patterns (2004)

name: Weekly Heikin-Ashi trend: long while the last completed weekly HA candle is green
rule: W = ctx.resample(bars,'1w') keeping only complete:true bars. For each weekly bar: haC = (o+h+l+c)/4; haO[k] = (haO[k-1]+haC[k-1])/2, seeded with (o+c)/2 of the first weekly bar. At daily bar i: ENTER long when the latest complete weekly HA candle is green (haC > haO) and the previous complete weekly HA candle was red. EXIT when the latest complete weekly HA candle is red. State changes only when a new weekly bar completes. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Weekly Heikin-Ashi is a widely shared swing/investor trend filter; with slow weekly flips it tests whether the HA colour on a slow timeframe beats the daily version in the registry.
source: Dan Valcu, Heikin-Ashi (2004); StockCharts ChartSchool 'Heikin-Ashi'

name: Keltner channel lower-band reversal: re-entry through the lower band after a close below it
rule: lower[k] = ctx.ema('close',20,k) - 2*ctx.atr(10,k). ENTER long on bar i when close[i-1] < lower[i-1] and close[i] >= lower[i] and close[i] > open[i]. EXIT when close[i] >= ctx.ema('close',20) or after 10 bars in the position. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: The registry has the Keltner breakout and a trend pullback; the lower-band fade (buying the close back inside after a volatility-adjusted flush) is the other common retail use.
source: Chester Keltner, How to Make Money in Commodities (1960); Linda Raschke 'Keltner/Bollinger' band-reentry notes

name: STARC bands (Stoller): buy a close below SMA(6) minus 2 ATR(15), exit at the SMA(6)
rule: lowerSTARC[i] = ctx.sma('close',6) - 2*ctx.atr(15). ENTER long when close[i] < lowerSTARC[i]. EXIT when close[i] > ctx.sma('close',6). Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: STARC bands are a retail-known volatility-envelope cousin of Keltner/Bollinger with a very short centre line; the registry has no STARC test.
source: Manning Stoller, Stoller Average Range Channels; StockCharts ChartSchool 'STARC Bands'

name: Bollinger %b below 0.05 confirmed by MFI(10) below 20 (Bollinger's own indicator pairing)
rule: %b = (close - lower)/(upper - lower), bands SMA20 +/- 2*sample std (ctx.rollingStd). TP = (H+L+C)/3; raw flow = TP*volume; MFI(10) = 100 - 100/(1 + sum of raw flow on up-TP bars over 10 / sum on down-TP bars over 10) (up/down by TP vs the prior TP). ENTER long when %b[i] < 0.05 and MFI[i] < 20. EXIT when %b[i] > 0.5. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Bollinger's book prescribes confirming band signals with a volume-based indicator such as MFI; the registry has %b and MFI separately but never in this specified pairing.
source: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (2001), ch. on combining indicators (%b with MFI)

name: True Strength Index (25,13) signal cross while TSI is above zero
rule: m[k] = close[k] - close[k-1]. TSI[i] = 100*EMA13(EMA25(m))/EMA13(EMA25(|m|)) (each EMA seeded with the SMA of its first inputs). signal = EMA7(TSI). ENTER long when TSI[i-1] <= signal[i-1], TSI[i] > signal[i] and TSI[i] > 0. EXIT when TSI[i] < signal[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: TSI is a common double-smoothed momentum oscillator with a built-in signal line; no TSI rule is in the registry.
source: William Blau, Momentum, Direction, and Divergence (1995), True Strength Index

name: Bull flag breakout: 15% ten-day pole, five-bar shallow flag, close above the flag high
rule: Let f=5, c0 = close[i-6] (last pole bar), c1 = close[i-16]. Pole: c0/c1 - 1 >= 0.15. Flag window = bars i-5..i-1: max high of the flag <= 1.02*max(high[i-16..i-6]); min low of the flag >= c0 - 0.5*(c0 - c1); (max high - min low of the flag)/c0 <= 0.15. ENTER long on bar i when close[i] > max high of bars i-5..i-1. EXIT when close < min low of bars i-5..i-1 (taken at entry) or after 15 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: The bull flag is the most-requested continuation pattern in retail crypto communities; fixed bar counts make it testable without discretion.
source: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed., 2005), flags; Edwards and Magee, Technical Analysis of Stock Trends

name: Fibonacci weekly pivot S2 reversion: buy a close at or below P - 0.618*range of last week, sell at P
rule: Use the last complete weekly bar from ctx.resample(bars,'1w') (complete:true): P = (H+L+C)/3, R = H - L. S2 = P - 0.618*R. ENTER long on daily bar i when close[i] <= S2. EXIT when close[i] >= P or after 14 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Fibonacci pivots are the second most common pivot variant after floor pivots; the registry has floor, Camarilla and CPR but no Fibonacci levels or an S2 fade.
source: Fibonacci pivot points, StockCharts ChartSchool 'Pivot Points' and Investopedia 'Fibonacci pivot points'

name: Anchored VWAP from the latest confirmed swing low: long on the cross above it
rule: Swing low at bar a: low[a] is the minimum of low[a-10..a+10]; it is known only from bar a+10. At bar i let a be the latest confirmed swing low (a <= i-10). TP=(H+L+C)/3; AVWAP(k) = sum_{j=a..k}(TP[j]*vol[j]) / sum_{j=a..k} vol[j] using this same a for k = i-1 and i. ENTER long when close[i-1] <= AVWAP(i-1) and close[i] > AVWAP(i). EXIT when close[i] < AVWAP(i). Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Anchoring VWAP to the last swing low is the standard retail 'who is in profit' line; the registry anchors only to the year start, 52-week high, months and fixed windows.
source: Brian Shannon, Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes (2008), anchored VWAP; Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade

name: Wilder extreme point rule: after a +DI/-DI cross buy the break of that day's high
rule: +DI/-DI as in Wilder (see ADX definition). ADX(14), Wilder: +DM = up move (high[k]-high[k-1]) if it exceeds the down move (low[k-1]-low[k]) and is > 0, else 0; -DM symmetric; TR, +DM, -DM smoothed with Wilder (first value = sum of the first 14, then S = S - S/14 + x); +DI = 100*S(+DM)/S(TR), -DI likewise; DX = 100*|+DI - -DI|/(+DI + -DI); ADX = first value mean of 14 DX, then (prev*13 + DX)/14. On a bar c where +DI crosses above -DI (+DI[c-1] <= -DI[c-1], +DI[c] > -DI[c]) set EP = high[c] (replacing any pending EP). ENTER long on a bar i > c when close[i] > EP and +DI[i] > -DI[i] with no -DI cross since c. EXIT when -DI crosses above +DI. A -DI cross above +DI cancels any unfilled EP. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Wilder's extreme-point rule is the original, discretion-free way to use a DI cross and is a different trigger from the immediate DI cross tested in the registry.
source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978), Directional Movement 'extreme point rule'

name: TEMA(10)/TEMA(30) cross: triple exponential moving averages
rule: TEMA(n) = 3*E1 - 3*E2 + E3, E1 = EMA_n(close), E2 = EMA_n(E1), E3 = EMA_n(E2), each seeded with the SMA of its first n inputs. ENTER long when TEMA10[i-1] <= TEMA30[i-1] and TEMA10[i] > TEMA30[i]. EXIT when TEMA10[i] < TEMA30[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: TEMA is the common retail low-lag moving average; the registry has Hull, ALMA, KAMA and T3 but not DEMA/TEMA.
source: Patrick Mulloy, 'Smoothing Data with Faster Moving Averages', Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities (Jan 1994)

name: Inside week breakout: close above the high of a completed inside week, exit on a break of its low
rule: Weekly bars from ctx.resample(bars,'1w'), complete:true only. Let w = the last complete week and p the week before it. Inside week: high[w] <= high[p] and low[w] >= low[p]. During the week immediately after w (the incomplete week), ENTER long on daily bar i when close[i] > high[w]. EXIT when close[i] < low[w] or after 5 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Inside bars are tested on the daily chart; the inside-week variant is a lower-noise swing version popular in forex and index communities.
source: Price-action education (Nial Fuller, Learn To Trade The Market); Crabel-style compression, Toby Crabel, Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns (1990)

name: Regular bullish RSI(14) divergence on daily confirmed pivots
rule: RSI = ctx.rsi(14). A pivot low at bar p is confirmed at bar p+K when low[p] is strictly below the K lows before and the K lows after it (K=3 here), so it is known only from bar p+K onwards. At confirmation bar i = p+3 of pivot low p, let q be the previous confirmed pivot low with 8 <= p-q <= 40. ENTER long when low[p] < low[q] and RSI[p] > RSI[q] and RSI[q] < 35. EXIT when RSI[i] > 55 or after 20 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: RSI divergence is the single most-taught retail reversal signal; only the hourly crypto version is in the registry.
source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); Cardwell/Brown, RSI: The Complete Guide (2000)

name: Hidden bullish RSI(14) divergence in an uptrend: higher price low with a lower RSI low
rule: RSI = ctx.rsi(14). A pivot low at bar p is confirmed at bar p+K when low[p] is strictly below the K lows before and the K lows after it (K=3 here), so it is known only from bar p+K onwards. At confirmation bar i = p+3 of pivot low p, let q be the previous confirmed pivot low with 8 <= p-q <= 40. ENTER long when low[p] > low[q], RSI[p] < RSI[q], RSI[p] < 50 and close[i] > ctx.ema('close',200). EXIT when close[i] < low[p] or after 20 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Hidden divergence is the retail trend-continuation counterpart to regular divergence and is a common pullback-entry rule.
source: Cardwell/Brown, RSI: The Complete Guide (2000) positive/negative reversals; Constance Brown, Technical Analysis for the Trading Professional (1999)

name: Hourly Stochastic RSI (14,14,3,3) cross up from below 20 above the 200 EMA
rule: r = ctx.rsi(14); S[i] = (r[i] - min r[i-13..i])/(max r[i-13..i] - min r[i-13..i]) (0 if max=min); K = 100*SMA3(S); D = SMA3(K). ENTER long when K[i-1] <= D[i-1], K[i] > D[i], K[i] < 20 and close[i] > ctx.ema('close',200). EXIT when K[i] >= 80 or after 48 bars. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Stochastic RSI with a 200 EMA trend filter is a top-shared hourly crypto scalp recipe; the registry has the unfiltered daily version only.
source: Tushar Chande and Stanley Kroll, The New Technical Trader (1994), StochRSI; TradingView community hourly scalp scripts

name: Cumulative RSI(2) (Connors): two-day RSI(2) sum below 35 above the 200-day SMA
rule: r = ctx.rsi(2). cum[i] = r[i] + r[i-1]. ENTER long when cum[i] < 35 and close[i] > ctx.sma('close',200). EXIT when r[i] > 65. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Cumulative RSI is Connors' improvement on single-day RSI(2), which the registry tests on BTC; the 2-day sum is meant to need a deeper two-day flush.
source: Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), cumulative RSI

name: EMA 20/50 cross accepted only when ADX(14) is above 25
rule: ADX as defined below. ADX(14), Wilder: +DM = up move (high[k]-high[k-1]) if it exceeds the down move (low[k-1]-low[k]) and is > 0, else 0; -DM symmetric; TR, +DM, -DM smoothed with Wilder (first value = sum of the first 14, then S = S - S/14 + x); +DI = 100*S(+DM)/S(TR), -DI likewise; DX = 100*|+DI - -DI|/(+DI + -DI); ADX = first value mean of 14 DX, then (prev*13 + DX)/14. ENTER long when ctx.ema('close',20) crosses above ctx.ema('close',50) (prev <=, now >) and ADX[i] > 25. EXIT when EMA20 < EMA50. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: 'Only trade crosses when ADX shows a trend' is the standard retail filter; the registry gates Donchian and RSI with ADX but not a plain moving average cross.
source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); retail 'ADX filter' guides (StockCharts ChartSchool 'ADX')

name: Double Bollinger Bands (Lien): buy a close entering the +1 to +2 sigma buy zone, exit at the mean
rule: m = ctx.sma('close',20), s = ctx.rollingStd('close',20). ENTER long when close[i] > m+1s, close[i] <= m+2s, and close[i-1] <= m[i-1]+1s[i-1]. EXIT when close[i] < m[i]. Conventions: signal(bars,i,ctx) uses only bars[0..i]; long only; returns 1 while the position is open, else 0; ENTER/EXIT are evaluated on the close of bar i (no fill before bar i+1); ENTER is ignored while in a position; indicators return NaN until warm and no signal is produced then; ctx.sma/ema/rsi/atr/donchian are the harness helpers (Wilder RSI/ATR, EMA seeded with the SMA).
rationale: Kathy Lien's Double Bollinger Bands treat the +1 to +2 sigma zone as a trend buy zone, the opposite reading to the lower-band mean reversion that dominates the registry.
source: Kathy Lien, Day Trading and Swing Trading the Currency Market (2008), Double Bollinger Bands
